We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a template (733) that disconnections sulfonamide: product is sulfonamide linking aryl sulfonyl chloride with an aniline. The retro template: Cl-SO2-Ar + NH2-Ar' -> Ar-SO2-NH-Ar'

Our target has sulfonamide linking two aryl groups: left aryl is p-tolyl (CH3 on phenyl) attached to N of sulfonamide; right aryl is phenyl with a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (i.e., an anilide with a trans-alkene). So we can disconnect at sulfonamide: left side aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and right side aniline (aryl amine) that is the other aryl with side chain.

Thus step 1: Use template 733 to break sulfonamide into two precursors:

- Precursor A: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1) (or maybe ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1). Check buyability.

- Precursor B: aniline with side chain: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., 4-(E-... ) aniline). Actually the aniline is attached via NH to sulfonyl, so the amine is the aryl with side chain and an NH (i.e., aniline). So precursor B is the aryl amine: c2ccc(N)cc2 with side chain? Wait the side chain is attached to the aromatic ring via the alkene? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. This is a phenyl ring with a para substituent of the side chain (trans-alkenyl amide). The amine is the aniline (NH attached to sulfonyl). Actually the SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2) - the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl at position 1 (the N). So the phenyl has N attached to sulfonyl, and also a para substituent of the side chain. So the aniline is the phenyl with side chain.

Thus we need to get that aniline via a prior step: maybe from a protected aniline (e.g., nitro reduction) or from a coupling.

Simplify: we can propose two-step route:

Step 1 (retro): target -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline (via template 733). That's one step.

Step 2: The aniline precursor (aryl amine with side chain) can be obtained by amide formation from aniline (without side chain) and an acid chloride of the side chain? Actually the side chain is C= C - C(=O)N- phenyl-NH2 (i.e., an amide attached to a phenyl). The side chain includes an amide linking to another aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the side chain is an amide attached to a phenyl with an NH2 (aniline). So the whole side chain is: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the aniline (the central phenyl) has a para substituent that is a trans-alkenyl amide linking to an aniline.

Thus we could disconnect at the amide bond: using a template for amide formation (reverse of amide). The retro template would break amide into acid chloride (or acid) and amine. The template we saw earlier (reaction_id 733) is for sulfonamide. For amide, we need a template that breaks amide to acid chloride + amine. Search for amide formation.

Search templates with functional_groups_formed "amide". Already did earlier but got many irrelevant. Let's search for functional_groups_broken "acyl chloride" and formed "amide". Already did but got some templates. The first result (reaction_id 884884) seems to be amide formation from acyl chloride and amine, with alkene side chain? The retro template: [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C;D1;H2:5]>>... It seems to involve an amide attached to an alkene (alpha,beta-unsaturated). That matches our side chain: the amide attached to a trans-alkene. So we can use that template to disconnect the amide: the product is amide with alkene; reactants are acyl chloride (Cl-C(=O)-CH=CH-) and amine (aniline). So step 2: break amide into acyl chloride (ClC(=O)CH=CH-Ph?) Wait the acyl chloride would be ClC(=O)CH=CH-? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. The amide carbonyl is attached to the alkene carbon (alpha,beta-unsaturated). So the acyl chloride precursor would be ClC(=O)CH=CH- (i.e., acryloyl chloride) attached to phenyl? Wait the alkene is attached to phenyl ring: /C=C/ attached to phenyl? The SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. The alkene is attached to the phenyl ring (the phenyl with side chain). Actually the side chain is phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Let's parse: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (ring B) has a substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So the substituent is a trans-alkenyl carbonyl attached to an aniline (c3...). So the carbonyl is attached to the alkene carbon (alpha,beta-unsaturated amide). So the acyl chloride would be ClC(=O)CH=CH- (acryloyl chloride) attached to phenyl? Actually the alkene is attached to the phenyl ring at the carbon of the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-. So the acyl chloride would be ClC(=O)CH=CH-Ph? Wait the phenyl is attached to the alkene carbon, not the carbonyl. So the acyl chloride is ClC(=O)CH=CH-Ph (i.e., 3-phenylacryloyl chloride). That is commercially available? Possibly not. But we could consider alternative: we could form the amide via coupling of aniline with acryloyl chloride (CH2=CH-COCl) then later do a Suzuki coupling to attach phenyl? But we need max 3 steps.

Alternative: we could disconnect the alkene formation (C=C) via a Heck coupling between aryl halide and acrylate? But limited steps.

Simplify: maybe we can propose a route where we first make the aniline with side chain via amide formation between aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acryloyl chloride, then do a Suzuki coupling to attach the phenyl ring (c2ccc...). However that adds steps.

Given max 3 steps, we can have:

Step 1: Sulfonamide formation (template 733) from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline with side chain.

Step 2: Amide formation (template for amide) from acryloyl chloride and aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give the side chain amide (i.e., 3-phenylacrylamide). But we also need the phenyl ring attached to the alkene (the phenyl that carries the sulfonamide). Actually the phenyl with sulfonamide is the same phenyl that has the side chain attached. So the amide formation yields the side chain attached to that phenyl. So the amine used is the phenyl with sulfonamide? Wait the amide is attached to the phenyl (the same phenyl that later will be sulfonylated). So the amide formation step would be between that phenyl (bearing the sulfonamide later) and acryloyl chloride? But the phenyl already has sulfonamide N attached; the amide carbonyl is attached to the alkene which is attached to that phenyl. So the phenyl is not the amine; the amine is the aniline (c3ccccc3N) at the end of side chain. Actually the amide is -C(=O)N- attached to phenyl (c3...). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3...). So the amide formation is between acryloyl chloride and aniline (c3...). That yields acryloyl anilide (CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). Then this acryloyl anilide is attached via the alkene to the other phenyl (the sulfonamide phenyl) via a cross-coupling (e.g., Heck). That would be step 3.

Thus route:

Target -> step1: sulfonamide formation from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aryl amine (which is phenyl with side chain attached via alkene). So we need that aryl amine (phenyl with side chain) as precursor.

Step2: that aryl amine can be obtained via Heck coupling between p-halophenyl (e.g., 4-bromo-? Actually the phenyl that will become sulfonamide has a para position for side chain; we need to attach the side chain via Heck between 4-bromo-? and acryloyl anilide. So we need a bromophenyl sulfonamide? Wait sulfonamide not yet formed. The phenyl that will later be sulfonylated is currently an aniline (NH) attached to sulfonyl later. So before sulfonylation, we have an aniline (NH2) on that phenyl. So we need a phenyl with NH2 and a bromide at para position to do Heck with acryloyl anilide. That is 4-bromo-2-methylaniline? Actually the phenyl has a methyl (para to sulfonamide). The target phenyl is p-tolyl (CH3 at para) attached to sulfonamide at position 1, and side chain at position 4? Wait the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. The left phenyl (with methyl) is attached to sulfonamide at position 1 (the N). The right phenyl (c2) is attached to sulfonyl at position 1 (the sulfonyl attaches to that phenyl). The side chain is attached to that right phenyl at para position (relative to sulfonyl). So the sulfonyl phenyl is the one with side chain. The left phenyl is p-tolyl attached to N of sulfonamide. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to left phenyl (p-tolyl). The sulfonyl group attaches to right phenyl (which also has side chain). So the sulfonamide formation step uses left phenyl sulfonyl chloride and right phenyl amine (the right phenyl has NH2). So the right phenyl amine is the aniline that will later have side chain attached via Heck.

Thus step 2: we need to synthesize that right phenyl amine (4-(E-... )-2? Actually the right phenyl has no methyl; it's just phenyl with side chain at para. So we need 4-bromo-? Actually we need aniline (NH2) at position 1, side chain at para. So we can start from 4-bromo-2? Wait there is no other substituent. So we need 4-bromo-aniline (p-bromoaniline) then do Heck coupling with acryloyl anilide to install side chain at para. That yields the right phenyl amine with side chain. Then step1 sulfonamide formation with left phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus steps:

Step A (retro): target -> left phenyl sulfonyl chloride + right phenyl amine with side chain.

Step B (retro): right phenyl amine with side chain -> p-bromoaniline + acryloyl anilide (via Heck reverse). The template for Heck coupling? We need a template that forms C=C bond between aryl halide and alkene. Search for functional_groups_formed "C-C double bonds" and broken "aryl halide".
